note: A `pin` takes the rules of a `turn` (SPEC 3.3.3, 6.2): it is a position on the arc, longitude and latitude only, and never a node key. Highlight 0 pins a pass with a position that carries an elevation: the channel is dropped, the pin and the highlight are kept, and `positions` pins the pin where it was written. Highlight 1 carries `pinned`, the key of the old boolean spelling, which this version does not recognise: it is skipped and reported, and the pass stays as it is, unpinned. Highlights 2 to 4 carry a pin that will not parse: a node key, the boolean `true` of the old spelling moved to the new key, and a latitude beyond 90. Each drops its highlight, because a walk with its pin removed reads as valid and is not the walk the user fixed, and each diagnostic names the `pin` key with the one code every unparsable position takes. A reader that still reads a boolean pin, or reads `pinned` as a pin, keeps a highlight here or misses a diagnostic.

diagnostics.message_advisory: a walk position carries longitude and latitude only — the elevation is dropped
`pinned` is not a key of a pass — skipped
`pin` is a string, expected a position — the highlight is dropped
`pin` is a boolean, expected a position — the highlight is dropped
`pin` has a latitude beyond 90 — the highlight is dropped
